_about: The Connected Era's six radio stations (Master Bible ch. 19). Station names and formats are the Bible's; programmes, hosts, songs, adverts and talk are the Connected Era's own. scripts/media/radio.py records every line and song listed here, and the Radio app reads the same file for its captions. Hours are local to the computer's clock; a programme whose 'to' is smaller than its 'from' runs past midnight.

spots.name: The Corner Bakery
spots.text: Mmm, smell that? It's the Corner Bakery on Main Street. Fresh bread every morning, cinnamon rolls every afternoon, and a free cookie for every kid who says please. The Corner Bakery. Come hungry.

spots.name: Pantry Recipes
spots.text: Stuck on what to make for dinner? Pantry Recipes has hundreds of easy recipes using things you already have in the cupboard. Find them at pantry recipes dot connected era dot local.

talk.text: The town library's summer reading club is going strong. Over two hundred kids have signed up so far, and the librarians say this year's most popular books are about dragons, spaceships and, for some reason, sandwiches. Sign-ups stay open until the end of August.

The Saturday farmers' market is back in the square, from eight until noon. This week, look out for strawberries, fresh bread, and the honey stand, which sold out by ten o'clock last week. Bring a bag and come say hi.
The public pool has extended its evening hours for the rest of summer. Lanes stay open until eight on weeknights, and Friday is family swim night, with music and a floating obstacle course.

In youth soccer, the under twelves played a cracking match on Saturday that finished three goals each. The coaches say everyone played their hearts out, and the oranges at half time were excellent. Next match is Saturday morning at the park.
Word around town is that the ice cream shop on Main Street is testing a new flavour. I'm told it involves cereal and marshmallows. I have volunteered to taste it. Purely for research, you understand.

Today we're asking: what's the best thing you've done this summer? So far we've heard about a backyard campout, a very competitive game of water balloon tag, and someone who finally learned to ride a bike at forty two. Good for you!
Back to school season is here. Crossing guards will be out from seven thirty, so please slow down near the schools. And to every student starting somewhere new this year, good luck. You'll do great.
The autumn harvest fair opens at the fairground this weekend, with a pumpkin weighing contest, hay rides, and the famous pie table. Last year's winning pumpkin was so big it needed its own wagon.
The town's leaf collection starts on Monday. Rake your leaves to the curb and the trucks will come by your street during the week. Or, you know, jump in them first. We won't tell.
In high school sports, the girls' volleyball team won their home opener in straight sets, cheered on by a gym full of very loud parents. Their next home game is Thursday night.

Halloween is coming, and the house on Maple Avenue has already started decorating. So far there are twelve pumpkins, one very large spider, and a skeleton wearing sunglasses. I can't wait to see what's next.
Today we're talking about comfort food. Callers have told us about grandma's soup, cheese toasties at midnight, and pancakes for dinner. That last one sounds like a very good idea.
If the snow keeps up tonight, the schools will announce any closures on the radio first thing in the morning. So keep TalkWave on, and keep your sledge somewhere you can find it.
The holiday lights in the town square will be switched on Friday evening at six, with hot chocolate from the bakery and carols from the community choir. Wrap up warm.
The community centre has started its winter classes, including beginner guitar, pottery, and something called extreme knitting. Sign-ups are at the front desk.

The outdoor ice rink is open again. Free skate is every afternoon from three, and the Saturday hockey games for the little ones are well worth watching. Mostly for the falling over, and the getting back up again.
I've been told there's a snowman on Birch Street wearing a full tuxedo and a top hat. Honestly, he's better dressed than I am. Send us your snowman stories.

This afternoon we're asking about new hobbies. One listener has started baking bread, another is learning the ukulele, and one gentleman is teaching his dog to skateboard. We'd love an update on that.
Saturday is spring cleanup day at the park. Gloves and bags are provided, and the bakery is bringing muffins for every volunteer. It's a great way to meet your neighbours.
The community garden has a few plots left for the season. If you've ever wanted to grow your own tomatoes, now's your chance. There's a beginner workshop on Sunday morning.
Little league baseball is back! Opening day is Saturday at the park, starting with the parade at nine. Bring a chair, bring a snack, and cheer for everybody.
Big news from the bakery on Main Street: they're adding a second croissant flavour. My sources say it might be chocolate and orange. I'll be standing outside on opening morning.

On today's show, we're talking spring plans. Listeners have told us about the first picnics of the year, garden makeovers, and a family who's planning a kite festival in their backyard. Sounds lovely.

A reminder that the town library has free wireless internet, and computers you can book for an hour at a time. The librarians are happy to help you set up an email account, if you've been meaning to get one.

Before the break, a quick shout out. A listener called to say a stranger helped carry her shopping all the way home yesterday. Whoever you are, thank you. Little things like that make a big difference.
The fun run is coming up soon, and this year's theme is superheroes. Capes are encouraged, walking is allowed, and there's a medal for everyone who crosses the finish line.
Apparently everyone on Birdie is talking about their lunch again today. I had a ham sandwich. Riveting stuff. You heard it here first, folks.
